question.text: A sealed flask with a capacity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>dm</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math> contains <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>11</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of propane gas. The flask is so weak that it will burst if the pressure becomes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>MPa</mi></math>. The minimum temperature at which the flask will burst is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mprescripts></mprescripts><none></none><mo>∘</mo></mmultiscripts></math>. [Nearest integer] (Given: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Atomic masses of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></math> are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi></math> respectively.) (Assume that propane behaves as an ideal gas.)

solution.text:
Real gases behave ideally at high temperature and low pressure.

Number of moles of propane gas, C3H8=1144=0.25 moles

PV=nRT

P=Pressure=2MPa

V=Volume=2dm3

n=Number of moles

T=Temperature

⇒2×106×2×10-3=0.25×8.3×T

⇒T=1927.710 K=1654.56 °C
